rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords may terminate tenancies only for listed just causes. At-fault causes include nonpayment, failure to cure a lease violation, nuisance or damage, illegal use, refusal to renew a similar agreement, denial of reasonable access, and an unapproved subtenant at lease end. No-fault causes include owner or family move-in, a required resident manager, demolition, removal from the rental market or conversion to non-residential use, a government order to vacate, a HUD sale, residential hotel conversion or demolition, and conversion to affordable housing. Landlords must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions. Applies to tenancies once the tenant has lived in the unit 6 months or the original lease has expired, whichever comes first.
rules.key_value: Just cause required for termination; relocation assistance for no-fault evictions
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the RSO, including buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and single-family dwellings.
rules.exemptions: Units regulated by the RSO, which has its own protections. Also exempt: transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity/sorority houses, the owner's roommate, cooperatives under certain circumstances, some non-profit homeless facilities or short-term substance abuse treatment centers, and some properties owned by HACLA or the government. Tenancy must be at least 6 months old or the original lease must have expired.
rules.interaction: Covers units not under the RSO; units covered by the JCO may also be subject to state AB 1482 rent caps.
rules.citation: L.A. Mun. Code ch. XVI, art. 5
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

rules.title: Los Angeles nonpayment eviction threshold (Fair Market Rent)
rules.requirement: For all RSO and JCO rental units, landlords may not evict a tenant for falling behind in rent unless the amount owed exceeds the Fair Market Rent (FMR) for the unit's bedroom size.
rules.key_value: No nonpayment eviction unless arrears exceed one month's Fair Market Rent for the bedroom size
rules.coverage_conditions: All RSO and JCO rental units in the City of Los Angeles.
rules.exemptions: Units exempt from both the RSO and the JCO.
rules.interaction: Applies alongside the JCO and RSO just cause provisions.
rules.quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482) rent cap
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases are limited to 5% plus the regional change in the cost of living, or 10%, whichever is lower. For the Los Angeles region the maximum was 8.9% for Aug 1, 2024 to Jul 31, 2025 and 8.8% for Aug 1, 2023 to Jul 31, 2024.
rules.key_value: 5% + regional CPI, max 10% per year (LA: 8.9% for Aug 2024–Jul 2025)
rules.coverage_conditions: Buildings older than 15 years (rolling); not units under local rent control (RSO).
rules.exemptions: Units built within the last 15 years (rolling); deed- or regulatory-restricted affordable units; certain dormitories; two-unit properties where the owner occupied the other unit for the entire tenancy; single-family homes and condos not owned by a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, where written notice of exemption was given; units subject to the City's RSO.
rules.interaction: Does not apply to units already subject to the Los Angeles RSO.
rules.quoted_span: rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region in which the property is located, or 10% whichever is lower
rules.conflict_note: Effective date derived from CA default rule (Act of 2019, no urgency clause stated); the document does not state an effective date.

no_rule_findings.finding: The Los Angeles JCO itself does not regulate rent increases; JCO-covered units may instead be subject to state AB 1482.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The JCO does not regulate rent increases
